reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about the role of Cr and Al in forming protective oxide scales and their effect on oxidation resistance in multiprincipal-element alloys, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these key premises.
premises: Higher Cr and/or Al content enables formation of more protective oxide films (Cr2O3/Al2O3) in multiprincipal-element alloys.
These protective oxide scales slow oxygen diffusion and reduce internal oxidation.
The oxide scales are adherent and self-healing upon minor damage.
Alloys with increased Cr/Al will develop thicker, more adherent, and slower-growing protective oxide scales compared to lower-content alloys.
This results in lower oxidation weight gain and improved retention of mechanical properties.
